ENVELOPE WRITTEN 2026-09-10T00:15:48Z (version CreatedDate, AWS-side). SIGNING DID NOT MOVE UNTIL 01:09:42Z. Every reading below sits between those two, so the overlap is demonstrated BEFORE the switch rather than reconstructed after it.

'DEPLOYED IS NOT SERVING' IS SATISFIED IN THE STRONG DIRECTION: every read above is against the live wire, and CloudTrail was explicitly REFUSED as the instrument -- it showed 0 GetSecretValue events after the write, which is delivery latency and not convergence evidence. For the replicated edge the read is a request that actually traverses it.

NO CONSUMER WAS REDEPLOYED DURING THE WINDOW, measured on LastModified rather than asserted: session-analytics 2026-09-09T21:26:02Z, portal-authorizer 18:50:07Z, auth-handler 23:39:18Z, auth-validator-edge 19:43:47Z -- ALL PREDATE the 00:15:48Z envelope write. So each acceptance is a deployed artifact re-reading a CHANGED SECRET on its TTL, which is the property the rotation depends on, and not a fresh deploy that would have masked whether convergence works at all.

*** A FALSE FAILURE WAS CAUGHT HERE AND IT WOULD HAVE HALTED A CORRECT ROTATION. *** The first session-analytics probe (00:29Z) read NEW accepted / OLD REJECTED -- the exact signature of a single-slot verifier. The fixture had aged out mid-experiment: the old-key token carried exp 00:28:16Z and was presented 342s past it while the new-key token was still live. AN EXPIRED TOKEN AND A WRONG-KEY TOKEN BOTH RETURN 401 {"error":"Unauthorized","details":"Invalid token"}, BYTE-IDENTICAL. Every arm was re-minted, and the EXP arm above exists so the record MEASURES that confound rather than asserting it was separated.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: NOBODY WAS SIGNED OUT, AND THIS IS THE OUTCOME'S OWN BAR: a token minted under the OLD key before the rotation, presented AFTER the signing switch, still verifies -- request, response and the token's identity and expiry pasted at each step. **NEGATIVE CONTROL: a token signed by a key that was never in either slot is REFUSED**, so the acceptance is not measuring "everything passes".
acceptance.invocation: POST https://opalinvest.dev/auth/refresh with Cookie: refresh_token=<the L1 artifact>, at 01:21:40Z
acceptance.output_evidence:
METHOD: Present the LITERAL pre-act token -- the artifact minted at L1 before any secret was written, unchanged on disk -- after the switch. Its 7-day refresh lifetime is why it survives as evidence where a 15-minute access token cannot.

THE LOAD-BEARING ARM USES THE ORIGINAL ARTIFACT, NOT A RE-MINTED STAND-IN.
  token identity : sub baef282ac2679e74107266bab569a856, email s10-preact-probe@opalinvest.com, type refresh
  minted         : iat 1788999196 = 2026-09-10T00:13:16Z -- BEFORE the envelope write (00:15:48Z) and
                   BEFORE the signing switch (01:09:42Z)
  expiry         : exp 1789603996, with 600696s still to run at the time of the request
  signed by      : the OLD private key, verified locally -- verifyWith(token, oldpub) = true
  request        : POST https://opalinvest.dev/auth/refresh, Cookie: refresh_token=<token>, body {}
  response       : HTTP 404 {"error":"User not found"}

'User not found' IS THE ACCEPT, and it is L1's pre-act baseline discriminator unchanged: the signature VERIFIED and the request then failed at the user lookup because the sub is a fabricated opaque binding with no row. The REJECT answer on this same axis is {"error":"Internal server error"}. Calibrating that pair BEFORE the act is what makes this reading mean anything -- 'the old token still verifies' is worth nothing unless it verified before, and a probe failing for a non-crypto reason at both ends would have looked identical to success.

A REAL SESSION CROSSING THE SWITCH, end to end, 01:21:40Z: an OLD-key refresh token for an ACTIVE account -> HTTP 200, and the returned accessToken verifies [oldpub=false newpub=true]. A client holding a PRE-ROTATION token is admitted and handed a token signed by the POST-ROTATION key. That is the whole outcome in one exchange.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, RUN IN THE SAME PASS AND REFUSED EVERYWHERE: a token signed by a keypair generated fresh for the purpose -- so it is provably not the old key under another name -- was refused at every consumer. /auth/refresh -> HTTP 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}; edge+authorizer -> 401; session-analytics -> 401 Invalid token. And the EXP arm (the CORRECT old key, deliberately expired) was refused with BYTES IDENTICAL to the CTL arm, which is what separates 'the old key no longer verifies' -- a rotation failure -- from 'my fixture expired again'.
acceptance.denominator: 1 pre-act artifact re-presented post-switch + 1 live-account session + 2 refusal controls (CTL, EXP) at 3 surfaces

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: THE NEW KEY IS ACTUALLY THE ONE SIGNING: a login performed after the switch yields a token whose header/key-id resolves to the NEW key, pasted; and the old key is confirmed still present as a verification slot at that moment. **A rotation nobody can observe on the wire has not been demonstrated.**
acceptance.invocation: POST /auth/refresh (returns an accessToken from generateAccessToken -> getJwtPrivateKey), then crypto.createVerify('RSA-SHA256') against oldpub.pem and newpub.pem
acceptance.output_evidence:
METHOD: SUBSTITUTE ORACLE, and it is stronger than the one the criterion names. These tokens carry NO key-id: the header is {"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT"} and every consumer calls jwt.verify with key material rather than a kid lookup, so 'header/key-id resolves to the NEW key' is not expressible on this wire. Instead the minted token's SIGNATURE is verified locally against each public half -- which settles WHICH PRIVATE KEY SIGNED IT as a cryptographic fact rather than as a label the signer asserts about itself.

OBSERVED ON THE WIRE, WITH A BEFORE AND AN AFTER ON THE SAME INSTRUMENT:
  00:56:01Z (pre-switch)  minted accessToken -> signed by OLD key [oldpub=true  newpub=false]
  01:16:32Z (post-switch) minted accessToken -> signed by NEW key [oldpub=false newpub=true]
  claims at both: sub=michael@opalinvest.com role=admin firmId=opal-capital, ttl 902s
  CTL at both vintages: a refresh token signed by a key in NEITHER slot -> HTTP 500, REFUSED

THE BASELINE IS WHAT MAKES THIS EVIDENCE. Without the 00:56:01Z read, 'signed by NEW key' would be equally consistent with a signer that had always used it. The FLIP on one unchanged instrument, with the control holding at both ends, is the demonstration.

WHY THIS IS A SIGNER OBSERVATION AND NOT AN INFERENCE FROM THE VERIFIERS (issuer condition 5): the returned accessToken is produced by generateAccessToken -> getJwtPrivateKey, so it is signer output by construction, and the verification is done LOCALLY in the probe. No verifier participates in the reading at any point.

THE OLD KEY IS STILL A VERIFICATION SLOT AT THAT MOMENT, measured in the same pass rather than assumed: at 01:21:40Z an OLD-key bearer returned 200 at the edge+authorizer and 400-past-the-gate at session-analytics, and the served envelope's `previous` slot fingerprints to 3051443047acf258... = oldpub.pem on SPKI DER.

THE ROUTE USED IS A LOGIN-EQUIVALENT, stated plainly: /auth/refresh rather than /auth/login, because the committed credential returns 200 mfaRequired with a challengeId and the MFA leg cannot be completed by this lane. /auth/refresh runs the SAME generateAccessToken path and is a live production route, so the signing read exercised is identical.
acceptance.denominator: 2 signer observations (pre and post) + 1 control at each + 2 confirmations that `previous` still verifies

mutant.description: The claim this face stands on is that every consumer ACCEPTS both slots and the signer MOVED to the new key. The reading that would make that claim look true while being false is an acceptance path that accepts ANYTHING -- if the check were disabled or bypassed, every arm would return 200 and the rotation would read perfect. The planted control is a token signed by an RSA-2048 keypair GENERATED FRESH inside the probe run, so it is provably not the old key wearing another name, and it is presented on the identical route in the same pass as the real arms. A second control was added after the fact and matters more: the EXP arm, the CORRECT old key with exp in the past -- because an expired fixture and a wrong-key fixture return byte-identical refusals, and a stale one had already produced a false single-slot finding at 00:29Z that would have halted the rotation.
mutant.expected: CTL (neither slot) REFUSED at every consumer while NEW and OLD are ACCEPTED; EXP (correct key, expired) REFUSED with the same bytes as CTL; no-bearer REFUSED.
mutant.observed: CTL: /auth/refresh HTTP 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}; edge+authorizer 401; session-analytics 401 Unauthorized|Invalid token. EXP: edge+authorizer 401; session-analytics 401 Unauthorized|Invalid token -- BYTE-IDENTICAL to CTL, which is the point of carrying it. no-bearer 401. Meanwhile NEW and OLD were accepted at all four consumers at the same vintages. The refusal is also visible from the other side: the CloudWatch log for the CTL arm at 01:16:34Z reads 'ERROR Error: W6 [JsonWebTokenError]: invalid signature', so the refusal is a real signature rejection rather than a routing or parameter failure.

determinism.method: The full four-arm probe was run at two separate vintages either side of the signing switch -- pre-switch 00:39:44Z / 00:40:58Z and post-switch 01:21:40Z -- with identical arm structure and freshly minted fixtures each time, and the signer probe was run twice on the same instrument (00:56:01Z and 01:16:32Z). Repeatability is judged on whether the ACCEPT/REFUSE pattern holds, not on whether one number recurs.
determinism.observed: STABLE where it must be and MOVED only where the act moved it. Across both vintages: NEW accepted, OLD accepted, CTL refused, EXP refused, no-bearer refused -- at every consumer, unchanged. The ONE thing that changed is the signer's own key, which flipped OLD -> NEW between the two signer reads, which is the act itself. A probe that returned the same signer answer at both vintages would have been the failure.

declared_exclusions.item: Retiring the OLD verification slot -- the final clause of deliverable 2 ('and only after that retire the old verification slot').
declared_exclusions.reason: DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, because doing it now would cause the exact failure this face exists to prevent. Refresh tokens live 7 days (REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY = '7d'), so a token minted before the switch stays valid for a week and is verified against the `previous` slot. Removing that slot today signs out precisely the users the no-sign-out bar protects. The old key must remain in `previous` for at least one REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY window; that retirement is a separate cut and is recorded as such in the runbook.
Prohibited by deliverable 4 in terms. RotationEnabled is confirmed still unset on both secrets. This face configures no unattended rotation and makes no recommendation to.

surprises: NFRA_OPSEC202609-Z-S161: THIS FACE'S OWN WRITE DEFECT, AND IT REACHED PRODUCTION. Passing the PEM as one argv element through .tools/aws.cmd -- a Windows CMD batch shim that cannot carry an embedded newline -- stored 27 bytes while put-secret-value returned rc=0, a VersionId and ['AWSCURRENT']. The signing secret was INVALID IN PRODUCTION for 3m52s (01:09:42.364Z -> 01:13:34.378Z), fixed via boto3. Blast radius measured: 1 invocation in the window, a cold start, which returned before reaching getJwtPrivateKey (no ERROR logged, and the generic catch demonstrably does log). Second-order defect found and disarmed: the corrective re-write left AWSPREVIOUS pointing at the truncated version, converting the documented rollback into a second outage. class BLOCKING, hazard_standing ARMED, disarm_owner 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z.
